text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LIETUVOS RYTAS

- European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene condemned on Tuesday the initiative of Lithuania's Confederation of Industrialists to reestablish a financial and industrial union with counterparts in Russia, Belarus and Ukraine.
- Delegations from Latvia and Lithuania will continue negotiations in Vilnius on Thursday over their disputed sea border.
- Swedish mass media group Modern Times Group which belongs to concern Kinnevik acquired TELE 3 television.

- High ranking Lithuanian officials reassured a nuclear international safety panel they will do everything possible to impose the necessary security measures at Ignalina before the first reactor is opened after the annual maintainance shut-down.

- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta expects inflation to be 10-12 percent in 1997. He said their will be two price rises this year, when the government increases excises for alcohol, tobacco and petrol and when heating energy tarriffs rise.
RESPUBLIKA
- Defence Minister Cheslovas Stankevichius signed an order to allows only high-ranking officials to provide information to the media.
- The rector of Vilnius university Rolandas Povilionis said he may he a candidate in the presidential elections.
- Parliament decided on Tuesday to decentralise the energy sector before July.
- Hermis Bank intends to increase its share of the banking market to 20 percent before 2001.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- State control officials said the authorities of state-run Klaipeda Stevedoring cheat the state and violate laws.
VERSLO ZINIOS

- Textile market leader Utenos Trikotazhas plans to boost output and sales by 16 to 20 percent in 1997. The company had 3.7 million litas net profit in 1996, an increase of 400,000 litas on the previous year.

- The stock exchange hit record-high turnover on Tuesday when trade worth 18.12 million was made. The biggest bussines of 15.95 million litas was registered in the stocks of Baltija Ship Yard in bloc trading.
- Kraft Jacobs Suchard Lietuva has around 50 percent of the country's coffee market followed by Educho with over nine percent.
- The official reserves of the Bank of Lithuania increased in March by $18.9 million to $813.9 million.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom + 370 2 22 35 17
